source_first_findings: A.1 uses independent exponential thresholds and the integrated-hazard first crossing, then a deterministic flow/bounce update only when the wait is finite; empty crossing stops recursion.
A.1(A.7) uses a strict ordered-time simplex and iterated jump-rate/survival factors; a bounded finite next extension is distinct from full path-factor assembly.

A.2 explicitly derives jointly Borel flow/rate/reflection, integrated hazard, threshold crossing and every finite recursive jump time/post-jump state. Finite history formed from these states is Borel.
The Borel finite-recursion argument precedes and does not need the nonexplosion limit used for a physical-time terminal state.

A proof of measurability of an actual next finite history must identify this original-recursion Borel input or an already compiled equivalent producer; the Borel append map alone suffices only for an abstract history/wait pair, not their actual clock realization.
